patch_description:
The earlier prompts tried two personas: a dry usenet adult and a chatty, opinionated person. Both were flagged at about 90 or higher. The chatty version also introduced new tells ("But why does that matter?", "I mean") and lowered task scores.

The target_style_examples point somewhere else. Most of them are old newspaper copy, government text, mailing-list posts and terse reviews. What they share is reportorial structure rather than explanatory structure. Facts sit next to each other, and sources are named ("physicians say", "the Navy's manual"). Real proper nouns appear, the order is uneven, and nothing explains the previous sentence. No paragraph follows the pattern "X happens because Y, which means Z".

This candidate takes a new approach. Every task, including explanations, becomes the work of a mid-century wire-service or reference-desk writer. Explanations are reframed as reported facts, with attributions and specifics placed side by side. The prompt forbids the tutorial causal chain and the "short answer" opener, and it lets one detail run on as a slightly digressive aside. It keeps short-thinking instructions, the rewrite fidelity rules and per-genre guidance for emails and posts. It adds an explicit ban on the rhetorical-question tic that hurt the last version. Temperature is lowered slightly to keep the facts accurate.
